u0201.line: National Space Day (23 August) 2026 theme: 'Towards Viksit Bharat: Innovating, collaborating and Aspiring to Global Space Leadership'; main ceremony → Ahmedabad.

u0202.line: 16th Indian Organ Donation Day (3 August 2026): Best State Award → Tamil Nadu.

u0203.line: Varsha Ashok Aglave → first woman Director General of the Geological Survey of India (31 July 2026).

u0204.line: World Tiger Day → observed every year on 29 July.

u0205.line: National Security Adviser Ajit Doval selected for the Lokmanya Tilak National Award 2026 (20 July 2026).

u0206.line: Groundwater Week 2026 in Uttar Pradesh → observed from 16 to 22 July.

u0207.line: Indian-origin astronaut Anil Menon reached the International Space Station aboard Soyuz MS–29 (14 July 2026).

u0208.line: Padma awardee folk singer Teejan Bai of Chhattisgarh passed away (5 July 2026); famed for Pandavani, which sings Mahabharata stories.
u0208.hook: Pandavani = songs of the Pandavas, i.e. the Mahabharata.

u0209.line: International Booker Prize → renamed 'Bukhman International Booker Prize' from 2027 (with Bukhman Philanthropies); £100,000 split equally between author and translator.

u0210.line: International Day of Yoga 2026 (June 21) theme: 'Yoga for Healthy Ageing'.

u0211.line: Strict ban on single-use plastics and littering → ordered across Ladakh (June 19, 2026).

u0212.line: Constitutional expert Subhash C. Kashyap, former Secretary-General of the Lok Sabha, passed away aged 97 (June 4, 2026).

u0213.line: Producer Pahlaj Nihalani (CBFC Chairperson 2015–2017) died in Mumbai aged 76. Teens Vivaan Chhawchharia, Ariana Agarwal, Avyana Mehta (all 16) → Global Winner, Earth Prize 2026.

u0214.line: President Droupadi Murmu presented the 'President of India's Police Colour' to Sikkim Police (May 28, 2026).

u0215.line: Lance Havildar Harbhajan Singh and Naib Subedar Sujit Kumar Pradhan → UN Dag Hammarskjöld Medal (posthumous). International Day of UN Peacekeepers → May 29.

u0216.line: 2026 UNESCO/Guillermo Cano World Press Freedom Prize → Sudanese Journalists Syndicate (May 4, 2026); World Press Freedom Day → May 3.

u0217.line: PM Modi opened 594-km, 6-lane (expandable to 8) Ganga Expressway at Hardoi, UP (29 April 2026): Meerut (Bijauli) → Prayagraj (Judapur Dandu), through 12 districts.
u0217.hook: Ganga Expressway numbers: 594 km long, 6 → 8 lanes, 12 districts.
u0217.trap: Inaugurated at Hardoi, not at either end (Meerut or Prayagraj).

u0218.line: Singer Asha Bhosle, Lata Mangeshkar's sister, died aged 92. Books: 'Salman Khan: The Sultan of Bollywood' → Mohar Basu; 'Sab Par Ram Tapasvi Raja' → Ashutosh Agnihotri.

u0219.line: Sadhvi Niranjan Jyoti → new Chairperson of the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC) (March 2026).

u0221.line: UP Government: prize money for the Laxman Award and Rani Lakshmibai Award raised from ₹3.11 lakh to ₹10 lakh each (24 March 2026).
u0221.trap: ₹3.11 lakh = old amount; ₹10 lakh each = new amount.

u0222.line: Sahitya Akademi Awards 2025 announced in 24 Indian languages (16 March 2026); Hindi award → Mamta Kalia for memoir 'Jeete Jee Allahabad'.

u0223.line: 98th Academy Awards (2026 Oscars) → Los Angeles, USA: Best Picture 'One Battle After Another'; Actor Michael B. Jordan ('Sinners'); Actress Jessie Buckley ('Hamnet'); Director Paul Thomas Anderson.
u0223.hook: Best Picture and Best Director go together: 'One Battle After Another' by Paul Thomas Anderson.

u0224.line: Thanya C. Nathan → set to become Kerala's first visually impaired civil judge after clearing the Kerala Judicial Service Examination (10 Feb 2026).

u0225.line: 68th Grammy Awards → Los Angeles (1 Feb 2026): Song of the Year 'Wildflower'; Record of the Year 'Luther' (Kendrick Lamar and SZA).
u0225.trap: Song of the Year = 'Wildflower'; Record of the Year = 'Luther'. Don't swap them.

u0226.line: Renowned ecologist Madhav Gadgil passed away at the age of 83 (7 January 2026).

u0227.line: Raveena Tandon → PETA India's 2025 'Person of the Year' (December 2025).

u0228.line: Dr. Tessy Thomas → 2025 Dr. Paulos Mar Gregorios Award (30 Nov 2025).

u0229.line: Swaraj Kaushal, former Mizoram Governor and senior advocate, passed away aged 73 (4 Dec 2025). Books: 'Bharat: That Is India' → Abhijit Joag; 'The Eleventh Hour' → Salman Rushdie.

u0230.line: Shubhangi Dutt → Best Actress Award at the International Film Festival of Australia for 'Tanvi The Great' (Dec 2025).

u0231.line: 2025 International Emmy Awards: Best Actor → Oriol Pla; Best Actress → Anna Maxwell Martin (24 November 2025).

u0232.line: Justice Surya Kant → assumed office as the 53rd Chief Justice of India (24 November 2025).

u0234.line: ICC Player of the Month, September 2026: men → Shubman Gill (record fifth time); women → Shafali Verma (both India).

u0235.line: IOA's best Indian athletes at Aichi–Nagoya Asian Games 2026: female → archer Kumkum Mohod; male → wrestler Sujeet Kalkal (given Raja Randhir Singh Award).

u0236.line: 20th Asian Games 2026 → Aichi–Nagoya, Japan (19 Sept–4 Oct); mascot Honohon; motto 'Imagine One Asia'; India fourth, 85 medals (21 gold, 27 silver, 37 bronze); 2030 → Doha.
u0236.trap: Games' best athletes were Yu Zidi (China) and Puripol Boonson (Thailand); Kumkum Mohod and Sujeet Kalkal were India's best (IOA).

u0237.line: India won the Women's T20 Asia Cup 2026 (its eighth title), beating Sri Lanka by 72 runs at Dubai International Cricket Stadium (13 Sept 2026).

u0238.line: US Open 2026 women's singles → Elena Rybakina (Kazakhstan), beat Aryna Sabalenka (Belarus) 6–4, 5–7, 6–2; her third Grand Slam singles title.

u0239.line: Neeraj Chopra finished second in men's javelin at the Lausanne Diamond League 2026 with 88.05 metres (21 August 2026).

u0240.line: Arjuna Award 2025: 17 athletes, incl. chess → Vidit Santosh Gujrathi, Divya Jitendra Deshmukh; badminton → Treesa Jolly, Pullela Gayatri Gopichand; athletics → Tejaswin Shankar, Priyanka Goswami.
u0240.trap: These are the National Sports Awards 2025, announced in August 2026.

u0241.line: 23rd Commonwealth Games → Glasgow (23 July–2 Aug 2026), 74 nations; India fourth: 39 medals (13 gold, 17 silver, nine bronze); boxing best (seven gold); 2030 host → Ahmedabad.
u0241.trap: Mirabai Chanu = India's first gold of the Games (weightlifting, 48 kg); Asmita Dey = India's first-ever Commonwealth Games judo gold (also 48 kg).

u0242.line: FIFA World Cup 2026 (23rd; Canada, Mexico, USA; 48 teams, 104 matches) → Spain beat Argentina 1–0 (extra time), second title; Golden Ball Rodri; Golden Boot Mbappé (10 goals).
u0242.trap: Spain's first title was in 2010; 2026 is its second. England finished third.

u0243.line: Wimbledon 2026 men's singles title → Italy's Jannik Sinner (12 July 2026).

u0244.line: ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2026 → England and Wales (June 12–July 5, 2026).

u0245.line: 2026 French Open, Stade Roland-Garros, Paris: men → Alexander Zverev (first Grand Slam); women → Mirra Andreeva (Russia). Uber Cup 2026 → South Korea, beating China.
u0245.check: Q641 'Which team finished as the runner-up? France' does not fit the French Open singles items; some context seems missing.

u0246.line: ISSF Junior World Cup Rifle/Pistol/Shotgun 2026 → Cairo, Egypt (19–27 April 2026); India first in medal standings.
u0246.check: Q646 names 'Maharashtra' as runner-up team at an international ISSF event; looks wrong or misplaced.

u0247.line: Ranji Trophy 2025–26 → Jammu and Kashmir (first title); runner-up Karnataka.

u0248.line: SAFF U-19 Women's Championship 2026 → Pokhara, Nepal (31 Jan–7 Feb 2026); India won (third title); runner-up Bangladesh.

u0249.line: 10th ICC Men's T20 World Cup (7 Feb–8 March 2026) → hosts India and Sri Lanka; 20 teams; Italy's debut; India champion; Player of the Tournament → Sanju Samson.
